With regard to the reuse of discarded plastics, the Bureau has found that polyethelene, polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride, and polypropylene, which are over 85 percent of discarded plastics, can be separated and then reformed. Separation of the waste thermoplastics has been achieved using a combination of techniques. Waste polyvinyl chloride can be broken down into a valuable chemical reagent and char suitable for use as a fuel.
For the present analysis, the agency assumes that none of the additional plastics will be recycled.

Incineration and deposit in sanitary landfills provide the normal method by which to dispose of nonrecyclable wastes. The Society of the Plastics Industries, Inc. reports that burning 2 to 4 percent plastics with other refuse in incinerators does not damage the incinerators or significantly change the composition of the effluent gas. However, the agency recognizes the preliminary nature of the SPI study and neither endorses nor refutes this finding.
When deposited in sanitary landfills, plastics and other light objects tend to rise over a period of time.
